'''Alison Woollard''' (born 1968) is a British biologist. She is a lecturer in the Department of [[Biochemistry]] at the [[University of Oxford]]<ref name="googlescholar">[https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=alison+woollard Alison Woollard's publications in Google Scholar]</ref><ref name="scopus">{{Scopus|id=6701846015}}</ref> where she is also a Fellow of [[Hertford College, Oxford]].<ref name="birkbeck">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/dr-alison-woollard-ive-got-the-performing-bug-9020180.html |title=Dr Alison Woollard: 'I've got the performing bug' |date=2013-12-22 |work=The Independent |archive-date=2013-12-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131231030322/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/dr-alison-woollard-ive-got-the-performing-bug-9020180.html |url-status = live}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Woollard was born in 1968 in [[Kingston upon Thames|Kingston-upon-Thames]].{{cn|date=August 2022}}

Woollard was educated at [[University of London]], gaining her undergraduate degree in [[Biological Sciences]] in 1991 and gained her [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree at the [[University of Oxford]] on [[Schizosaccharomyces pombe|fission yeast]] supervised by [[Paul Nurse]] in 1995.<ref name="xmas"/><ref name="woollardphd">{{cite thesis |degree=DPhil |first=Alison |last=Woollard |title=Cell cycle control in fission yeast |publisher=University of Oxford |date=1995 |url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/primo_library/libweb/action/dlDisplay.do?docId=oxfaleph013717690 |author-link=Alison Woollard }}{{Dead link|date=June 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Academic career==
Woollard moved to the [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] in Cambridge in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b08g52z3|title=Alison Woollard on what she has learnt from mutant worms, The Life Scientific - BBC Radio 4|website=BBC|language=en-GB}}</ref>

She is currently the Academic Champion for Public Engagement with Research at the University of Oxford, a post which she has held since 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Support for Public Engagement {{!}} University of Oxford|url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/research/public-engagement/support-researchers|access-date=2021-04-28|website=www.ox.ac.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof. Alison Woollard appointed as Academic Champion for Public Engagement with Research|url=https://www.bioch.ox.ac.uk/article/prof.-alison-woollard-appointed-as-academic-champion-for-public-engagement-with-research|access-date=2021-04-28|website=www.bioch.ox.ac.uk|language=en}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
In 2013 Woollard presented the [[Royal Institution Christmas Lectures]].<ref name="xmas"/><ref name="Tales from the lobster tank">{{cite web|last1=Woollard|first1=Alison|last2=Gilbert|first2=Sophie|title=Tales from the lobster tank|url=http://www.rigb.org/blog/2014/april/lobster|website=RIGB|access-date=17 November 2016|archive-date=18 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161118100634/http://www.rigb.org/blog/2014/april/lobster|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Christmas lectures will address ethical challenges posed by genetics">{{cite news|last1=Sample|first1=Ian|title=Christmas lectures will address ethical challenges posed by genetics|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2013/aug/05/christmas-lectures-ethical-challenges-genetics|website=The Guardian|date=5 August 2013 |access-date=17 November 2016}}</ref> She has also been interviewed on the BBC radio programme [[The Life Scientific]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Life Scientific: Alison Woollard|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b08g52z3|access-date=2021-04-30|website=www.bbc.co.uk}}</ref>
